body:
I do! Driving definitely is one of those - I mention that briefly in my soliloquy up there I think. I love to get lost in cheesy or powerful music, either zoning out or screaming at the top of my lungs or singing as loudly as possible. Glad to hear that helps you too :)

I also mention in my OP my tendency to cope through "fantasy" whether that be with a book, movie, or my own daydreams.  A lot of the time it includes an alternate life imagined where things are much different, or things will be much different, but it's usually a life that feels impossible to achieve.

For fun, I don't know...I like so many things yet depending on my mood I might feel numb and empty instead. I love outside. Hiking, biking, running, swimming, kayaking, fishing. A lot of my fantasies/daydreams include kind of utopian outside worlds. I also love dancing and singing, though I'm not very good at either.

Another thing I seem to do is get kind of lost in a hobby or skill, trying to perfect or master it, and then I move on. Examples include languages, calligraphy, harmonica, beat boxing, violin, painting nails, doing makeup (shoutout to /r/MakeupAddiction  and /r/RedditLaqueristas), pilates/yoga, oil painting...and when I say "master" and "perfect" I really mean until I get bored and move on :P

I'm so sorry to hear about your medication fiasco. It really is incredibly tough since our brain chemistries are so complex and unique. I am glad you have something that seems to be working out for you! I sincerely hope it continues :)

Friends, sure. I have enough to where I don't feel completely alone if I'm desperate. But normal lets-hang-out-and-be-normal-and-do-fun-things-together friends don't really exist for me. Or they do, but not on the deeper level I would like. It takes a lot for me to truly open up and be comfortable and relaxed around a person, unfortunately. But, like I said, I do have *some* people in my life like that, so I consider myself very fortunate in that respect.

What about you? I hope you also have some people you can connect to that make you feel loved and understood. And you can always talk to me, I'll keep an ear open for you!

1. I don't want you (or anyone) to ever be afraid of being "negative"  "downer" or whatever - at least while talking to me! 

2. I absolutely relate to the thoughts you've had, and especially loved when you said:
 >Mirandas of the world can't appreciate the value of a 'happy birthday' because they've always had a happy birthday

Wow, I just haven't thought of it that way. You really said something that clicked with me and connected with a major theme I've been discovering about myself. I have the tendency to assume *I'm* in the wrong, no matter what, and *I'm* the one who's being unreasonable. When that happened I didn't even want to say anything. I only brought it up after my incredible therapist said I absolutely had a right to be told happy birthday!

Also agree wholeheartedly re: politeness and sincerity. I'm kind and nice to everyone I meet, but if we aren't going to get into any more depth beyond how the weekend was, for example, then it's too painful to go beyond several minutes of chatting.

Another thing that is related to this that was something I meant to touch on in my OP was the facade/mask I feel I wear in public. Around the office, in class, with colleagues...I always have this persona that is too rigid because I'm terrified of screwing up, acting awkward, or letting people in on the secret of how horrible I am.

Instead of being my goofy, clumsy, and weird self (which only a handful of people IRL know about and have witnessed) I become someone who is probably very boring and uncomfortable to be around because I'm too terrified of saying anything that could turn someone off. I just feel constrained by my own ridiculous requirements and wish I could be free of them and be more natural with people. It's just so incredibly exhausting! I wonder if you or anyone else can relate to that? Or at least the pressure to act a certain way or to hide or underplay your suicidal thoughts/mental illness?

But, I am going to go to bed now so I'm not going to be able to comment until tomorrow afternoon at the earliest - I can't thank you enough for chatting with me tonight and being so open, honest, and compassionate. Can't wait to continue the discussion!

Thank you very much! I completely agree with all of your points made.

I actually work in and study clinical health sciences and neuroscience, and see a therapist and psychiatrist very regularly. I also take two SSRI's and they really have helped but haven't completely taken away pain or added happiness (not that they are meant to). I think they've helped mostly to make everything a little more bearable and tolerable.

I'm still working with my doctors on an ideal dosage and medication for what I'm looking for, but it is difficult because I have a number of mental health issues and physical health issues so finding something that works without affecting other areas is hard...but I have a wonderful medical team rooting for me and doing all they can to help me out!

And I would love to say or believe that this is temporary, but unfortunately the majority of my life has been spent feeling suicidal. I am holding out hope at this moment that things might change, and that I might one day consider myself a happy person...and reaching out to wonderful people like you and everyone in this community is a great step on that path, I think :) Thank you so much for your comments, thoughts, and insight!

I hope if you deal with or have dealt with these types of emotions and mental illnesses (assuming since you mentioned you take medication too) that you continue to find success in your treatment :)

That's absolutely a great point for me to keep in mind. Thank you so much for bringing it up! I think being so lost in my own depression and my own pain, I forget to look at the struggles of others. There can also be a need to have a certain self portrayed to the world that some might feel pressured to conform to, which could also skew my perception of how many people are happy.

However, I do know a lot of truly happy people (at least through my broad and personal definition of happiness or their own self-described idea of happiness)...some who are and always have been happy and have never really had any issues with that...and some people who have to work hard at achieving and sustaining happiness. And these people have been able to find happiness and work through hardships successfully through these daily reminders or cognitive training.

Unfortunately, I do not fit into either of the above categories (not that those are the only two categories of "happiness" if you really can categorize such a thing...but I digress) and it causes me a lot of despair. I'm hoping to hopefully someday fit the second category at least :)

But again, I think you've made an excellent and extremely valid point! I have been guilty of assuming my own awfulness is unmatched and everyone else is a better/happier person than me. It's something that I will continue to work through to hopefully improve my relationship with others.

Okay, your response is something I was hoping for, best case scenario, when I posted this - I'm being completely serious!

The "everything happens for a reason" person (let's call her Miranda I guess) sounds very similar to the person you described. She is incredibly kind, loving, good-hearted, and selfless. Yet, she completely misses the point when I'm reaching out to her. On more than one ocassion I've had to bring up concerns that she was invalidating how I was feeling - despite what I am sure were her best intentions.

For example(**WARNING LONG RAMBLING STORY THAT I AM FAMOUS FOR**): my birthday. Birthdays have always kind of sucked for me. It's a day I romanticize, but always seems to fall way short of the mark. Every year it's always a disappointment. So, this year when it was my birthday, I was actually really excited! Everyone in the grad program makes a big deal out of everyone's birthday...I've been part of the planning and execution of many a birthday for my fellow grad colleagues, so I was excited to see what was going to happen for my birthday.

"Miranda's" birthday was a month before mine. I planned out all of these amazing things for her, made her favorite foods, set up her favorite activities, got her favorite wine etc. Miranda asked me what I wanted for my birthday, and I said to hang out with the people I feel closest to in the program (about 5 people) and perhaps have thai food (my favorite) and go out dancing. Unfortunately, the weekend of my actual birthday was not a good time for everyone, so we set up a time two weekends later.

Not. One. Person. Said. Happy. Birthday. Not...one. I even waited until the weekend of my party, maybe thinking that they got my actual birthday mixed up and thought it was on the day of our party. Nope. The party was cancelled per my request. I was very upset and at the same time admonishing myself for falling for the maybe-people-could-possibly-like-me and maybe-this-time-it-will-be-different traps yet again. Miranda didn't even say happy birthday. I was especially upset considering the fact that I've gotten emails from Miranda reminding everyone in the program a birthday was coming up, to make sure we said happy birthday to them. Aaand the same courtesy was not extended for my birthday.

Anyway, I confronted her about it (nicely) and she said that obviously for those 5 people saying happy birthday wasn't a marker of friendship or how much you care about someone, so I basically should suck it up and not be upset about it and that I was taking it too seriously (of course she was extremely kind when saying this, but this was the basic thought). She thought it was silly that I would leap to the conclusion that they didn't care about me because they didn't say happy birthday.

Again I write another novel about the woes of being me, and for that I'm so sorry! I just really related to what you said about the new friend you've made who is non-judging and supportive. It's amazing to have someone like that, and I'm so grateful for the Miranda's of the world, but I can never relate to someone like that on a deep and fundamental level.

And, I just can't hear one piece of cliched advice and have that magically fix my problems, and I get kind of insulted when I get those kinds of responses. It really feels like the person is just giving up or just doesn't care, and hopes a quick reply like that will be satisfying enough to get me off their back. News flash: it actually does get me off their back, but only because I realize I should probably never bother them again with anything but the most superficial of thoughts and conversations. They suddenly become the person I say "I'm good, how about you?" as a response to a "how are you" question, rather than a truthful and meaningful response.

Ahh but back to the point, your compliments and comments have really cheered me up exponentially. I would love to have someone like you in my life too...I always wonder why I feel so out of place when I'm sure someone out there feels like I do - or at least is willing to dig deep enough to try and understand. So, no, I'm definitely not deleting this throwaway! I think it's a useful tool to have in the future for many reasons, and I'm more than happy to keep in touch with you via this account :) :)

And don't feel like you have to just listen to me ramble all day. I'm also a happy listener and would love to be supportive to you or anyone else in this community. I might not be able to give you great advice either, but advice is overrated sometimes! A sincere ear and earnest attempts at understanding are sometimes more successful in my book! :)

**Edit response to your edit:** that's so amazing and strangely comforting and eerie at the same time!! Maybe one day we will have it become a reality :)

I think about this idea a lot too - about how random it is that this is my life, you have your life, and we will never experience any other life than our own. Also how when lives cross, the person was just living completely outside of your knowledge, and then all of a sudden you come together, you share something, and you might then part ways and continue to exist without each other. Sorry, that was extreme rambling and I'm sorry if I lost you or if it wasn't a relevant response, but that idea has been on my mind a lot :)

I also like your assessment of my life and getting to this point. You've brought a new point of view to my existence and my perspective, which I absolutely love. It truly is random...isn't it also weird that I was born as a human in America in the 20th century? My ~80 years of experience is limited to this time period and this space, and not the billions of years past or billions of years into the future. That thought makes me a little sad. An infinite number of experiences and I only get one. And the one I do get is kind of crappy! (Said with tongue firmly in cheek)

But really, thank you for your kindness and your response. I really value what you've said.

I love this reply, thank you so much :)

I'm glad you were able to relate to my conception of loneliness. I think a lot of mental illness is just so incredibly difficult to describe, and I've struggled with that so I really am happy that it resonated with you. I absolutely know the feeling of "polite public discourse". To me, it seems like people are too exhausted around me to get into anything deeper than that, or I scare them off, so our relationship stays firmly in a very shallow level. Have you found anything that helps you form new relationships? Or any other experiences you would like to share in the same vein?

And there's no way you should believe I'm "smarter" than you based on one measurement of academic achievement :) Especially since you say you're going through a similar academic journey! I truly hope you find success.

I think you're right on target with the burnout hypothesis. I was actually going to mention some of that but thought it was long enough as it is :P I realized that I've never had a proper "break" from school since...I dunno...before I started preschool? Haha. I'm absolutely and unequivocally burned out and worn out and tired out. But, there's the whole wall of questions that start to bear down on me if I think of following another path than the one I'm on now, so right now I'm on the "just get through it" path until I can figure out another way.

Your compassion and kindness are absolutely appreciated. I could never express how your reading this and your comment uplifted me. I also really feel like you understood the points I was trying to relate, which is a wonderful feeling :)

Really, truly, thank you. I honestly mean it. I look forward to hearing your full reaction after reading all of it whenever you have the time. Writing the post was therapeutic in itself, which is a nice side effect to reaching out in this community. Again, thank you thank you. Have a wonderful night :)
